title: FujiwaraChoki/supoclip
text: An open-source OpusClip alternative https://www.supoclip.com/ Fuck OpusClip. ... because good video clips shouldn't come with ugly watermarks or platform lock-in. SupoClip is an open-source, AI-powered video clipping tool. Give it a long video — a podcast, a talk, a stream VOD — and it finds the most viral-worthy moments, scores them, and renders them as vertical 9:16 clips with face-centered cropping, word-synced subtitles, hook titles, and optional B-roll. Inspect the code, self-host it, or use the hosted version. Self-hosting is free for noncommercial use and for individual creators, including on monetized channels. Companies, agencies, team use, and paid hosting require written permission from Shiori LLC. See it first: watch real clips SupoClip generated from a long-form interview, or follow the self-hosting tutorial to run it on your own machine. Ways to Use SupoClip Option Details Hosted web app www.supoclip.com — no infrastructure to run iOS app SupoClip on the App Store — the same hosted pipeline, from your iPhone Self-host Docker Compose setup below, or the step-by-step self-hosting tutorial — free for noncommercial use and for individual creators on their own hardware MCP server mcp/ — use SupoClip from Claude, Cursor, and other MCP clients REST API API keys from /settings/api-keys authenticate the backend directly — see the API reference Why SupoClip Exists OpusClip is genuinely good at what it does — AI clip selection, accurate captions, virality scoring. But your usage is metered by plan, some exports carry platform branding, and your content and workflows live on their servers under their terms. SupoClip gives you the same core pipeline without the leash: Self-hostable — run it on your own hardware, process as much as it can handle No watermarks — your content stays yours Open source — inspect the code, self-host as an individual creator, and share noncommercial forks under the license Hosted option — when you'd rather not manage servers, the cloud version is there Features YouTube, Twitch, Kick & uploads — paste a YouTube video, a Twitch VOD or clip, or a Kick VOD or clip, or upload your own file (live streams are not supported). Twitch and Kick download providers and the optional Apify fallbacks are set in docs/configuration.md AI clip selection — an LLM (Gemini, GPT, Claude, or a local Ollama model) picks the 3–7 most clip-worthy segments from the transcript Virality scoring — every clip gets hook, engagement, value, and shareability scores Smart vertical cropping — face detection keeps the speaker centered in the 9:16 frame Word-synced subtitles — AssemblyAI word-level timestamps, custom fonts, caption templates with animation styles Hook titles — an AI-written headline burned into the top of each clip's opening seconds B-roll & transitions — optional Pexels stock footage overlays and transition effects Built-in editor — trim, split, and merge clips, then export with platform presets (TikTok, Reels, Shorts) Direct publishing — connect your own YouTube, TikTok and Instagram accounts, then post or schedule clips from the task page Performance loop — views, likes, comments and shares flow back from each platform and steer future clip selection toward what works for your audience Real-time progress — live pipeline updates streamed to the browser while your video processes Quick Start You need Docker, an AssemblyAI API key for transcription, and one LLM provider key (Google, OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local Ollama). git clone https://github.com/FujiwaraChoki/supoclip.git cd supoclip Create a .env in the root with your keys: ASSEMBLY_AI_API_KEY=your_assemblyai_api_key LLM=google-gla:gemini-3-flash-preview GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_google_api_key Then start everything: docker-compose up -d First startup takes a few minutes; watch it with docker-compose logs -f. Once healthy, open http://localhost:3107, create an account, and start clipping. The backend API lives at http://localhost:8000 with interactive docs at /docs. The template sets FRONTEND_PORT=3107. Existing deployments without this setting keep port 3001; preserve that port if your production reverse proxy uses it. See the setup guide for custom ports and public URLs. To run fully local with Whisper and Ollama (including the Docker networking Ollama needs), see the self-hosting tutorial. To use a different LLM provider or configure the optional pieces (B-roll, analytics, emails, YouTube metadata), see the configuration guide. If something misbehaves, the troubleshooting guide covers the common failure modes. Documentation Everything beyond this page lives in docs/: Guide What it covers Setup Docker-first install, local development, first-run checklist Configuration Every environment variable, operating modes, provider options App Guide Screens, workflows, admin features, hosted vs self-host Architecture How the frontend, API, worker, queue, and pipeline fit together API Reference Backend endpoints, API keys, admin and billing routes Development Running locally without Docker, testing, contributing workflow Troubleshooting Fixes for the common ways things go wrong Community Join the SupoClip Discord to share your clips, swap editing tips, ask for help with self-hosting, or suggest a feature. Development & Testing The stack runs locally without Docker too — see development for the backend (uv + FastAPI + ARQ worker) and frontend (Next.js + pnpm) commands. The test suite spans pytest, Vitest, and Playwright, all reachable from the repo root: make test License Shiori LLC makes this release available under the SupoClip Noncommercial Source License, version 1.1. It permits noncommercial self-hosting and forks with attribution. Individual creators may also self-host SupoClip for their own monetized use without asking. Other commercial use, including use by companies and agencies, internal business use, client work, team use, paid hosting, and commercial redistribution, requires prior written permission from Shiori LLC. Send permission requests to support@supoclip.com. Earlier releases retain the rights they were released under. License FAQ This summary is for convenience. The LICENSE file is what applies. Can I monetize clips I make with SupoClip? Yes, if you are an individual creator: one person, running your own self-hosted copy for yourself. You can post the clips to your own YouTube, TikTok, Instagram Reels, Shorts, and other channels and earn from them through platform payouts, ads, sponsorships, affiliate links, memberships, and tips. You can also take part in clipping campaigns that allow you to clip the content and pay you for clips you post on your own channels. You don't need to ask first. Who still needs a license? Companies, agencies, and other organizations, including for internal use. Anyone using SupoClip for someone else's channels or brand, including freelancers paid to edit or clip for clients. Teams, or several people sharing one installation, for commercial work. Anyone offering SupoClip to others as a hosted or managed service, selling it, or redistributing it commercially. Using one person's account on behalf of a company does not make it individual use. How do I ask for permission? Email support@supoclip.com with who you are, who would use SupoClip, and what you want to do with it. Permission is given in writing. What about the hosted plans at supoclip.com? The hosted web app and iOS app are separate from this license. Your subscription and the terms of service cover how you can use clips you make there. Based on SupoClip.
